provenance: Official validator-plugin README, root LICENSE, workspace Cargo manifests and Redis messenger implementation inspected at commit 2615ce96bedaabb217e2e0f0dc875991f85507bf

discoveries: The Rust Geyser plugin sends filtered account/transaction/block/slot observations through a binary Plerkle serialization layer to a message bus; it is validator-side indexing infrastructure, not a public SYLPH client.

README describes configurable queue buffers, worker counts, selected confirmation level, and consumer retries. The Redis implementation, after times_delivered exceeds retries, places the entry in an ACK list and XACKs it; this removes it from the pending retry path rather than preserving an unresolved delivery for independent recovery. The stream entry may remain until trimming, so the precise finding is loss of consumer pending/retry visibility, not necessarily immediate XDEL.

The README's stated Solana minimum is 1.10.41+, but current plerkle Cargo pins agave-geyser-plugin-interface and solana-transaction-status 4.2.2. The docs are not a safe compatibility contract. Root license is AGPL-3.0.

sources.overlap: The plugin's validator buffer and Redis consumer are a separate producer/transport architecture. provenance: Official Streamling Community Plugins README, Cargo metadata, S2 sink implementation, and S2 reader implementation inspected at commit 834657a18ff07d96a758165df698d12453e09159.
discoveries: The repository is a Rust FFI plugin package, not a Solana RPC/Geyser source; it contains storage/CDC plugins including S2 source and sink implementations.

The S2 sink submits records to a producer and uses checkpoint markers as durability barriers: it awaits outstanding record tickets before the host may acknowledge a checkpoint; retry/restart behavior is explicitly at-least-once and can duplicate records.

The S2 reader uses a bounded channel for backpressure, per-stream emitted sequence positions, and only prunes prefix-discovered readers after a complete listing scan; the package root license is FSL-1.1-ALv2 Future License.
patterns: separate enqueue acceptance from durable acknowledgement and advance a checkpoint only after all preceding writes are confirmed
make replay duplicates explicit and require idempotent sinks

sources.overlap: Checkpoint/ack patterns overlap conceptually with SYLPH's canonical journal and projection ACK transaction; the Rust Streamling/S2 stack is a separate ETL runtime and is not a Solana truth source.
risks: FSL-1.1 has competing-use restrictions and is not treated as an ordinary permissive license
at-least-once delivery can duplicate writes after ambiguous append outcomes
S2 checkpoint semantics cannot be substituted for SYLPH's transaction journal or recovery certificate
validation: before adapting the pattern, prove journal append, projection commit and ACK are ordered in one transaction or equivalent durable protocol
fault-inject ambiguous writes and restarts to measure duplicates and cursor movement
review FSL terms and avoid introducing an unnecessary Rust runtime dependency

provenance: Official Radiance repository README, Bigtable backfill notes, CAR creation metadata-filler and slot-range helper inspected at commit 53b06cb80250bb758677a26bbcabb670da88a8ee.
discoveries: The repository is an Apache-2.0 Go toolkit for Solana protocol/blockstore work; it can build CAR archives from RocksDB blockstores and backfill missing transaction metadata from Bigtable.

The metadata filler checks supported encodings, parses and reserializes transaction metadata, then sanity-decodes it; in the bincode path, nil metadata is logged and skipped, so callers still need a block completeness check.
Its slot-range helper sorts and deduplicates the provided slice in place before splitting work, which is useful for deterministic batches but mutates caller-owned input.

provenance: Official Orbshred README, MIT license, and source aggregation/registry/drop-counter code inspected at commit c5907afcd0baa54591bc950ebc4d4b787f9858ec.
discoveries: Orbshred compares identical `(slot, index, shred_type)` arrivals across raw UDP, Linux AF_PACKET, Jito ShredStream, DoubleZero, and Yellowstone sources; Linux packet paths use SO_TIMESTAMPNS while Yellowstone uses userland delivery time, so those measurements are not directly comparable.

Its aggregator uses bounded channels and increments per-source counters when try_send fails; the README explicitly warns these drops undercount observed source delivery and can make measured throughput incomplete.
The repository is MIT-licensed and is a local measurement tool, not a transaction decoder or canonical feed.

provenance: The manifest URL https://github.com/rpcpool/yellowstone-vixen resolves to solana-rpc/shipstern; both remote HEADs resolve to commit 1b6902bd949cf044b08c02d975002db0b3b837ae. discoveries: The renamed Shipstern project is an MIT Rust framework for Yellowstone-backed Solana pipelines with pluggable parsers/handlers, IDL-based parser generation, and Prometheus instrumentation; it is not the original repository identity anymore.

Its Yellowstone client can reconnect from the last seen slot and deduplicate replayed events, but its own configuration docs state that gap-free recovery requires server-side replay_stored_slots support.

Its dynamic filter-update docs describe a recoverable ResourceExhausted rejection that can cause the same refused filter to be resubmitted indefinitely; provider limits must be validated before sending updates.

provenance: Official @solsonar/solana-shred-parser README, package metadata, LICENSE, and ShredParser.js implementation inspected at commit 341651589b6a64b99a133d5367ecb75dcfbb777c.
discoveries: The MIT Node package reconstructs VersionedTransaction objects from the contiguous data-shred prefix before confirmed RPC arrival, but explicitly does not recover missing data from coding/FEC shreds or resolve ALT keys.

It emits transactions before slot close/confirmation and has no DEX decoding or canonical fork reconciliation, making it an early observation source rather than trade truth.

provenance: Official Solana Microscope README, root MIT license, Cargo workspace, event processor and telemetry implementation inspected at commit fb225510424acc349446d1d2f4d6f7c2dc40dc4.
discoveries: Microscope consumes confirmed transactions through Yellowstone gRPC or JSON-RPC and decodes configured programs with Carbon; it is self-hosted monitoring, not a market-data or execution service.
When its program-events feature is enabled, rejected log/CPI event decodes are emitted with source, program, instruction, signature and slot context and increment a dedicated Prometheus counter.

It separates established-stream disconnect/missed-slot counters from a Yellowstone probe-health signal, explicitly documenting that a flat disconnect counter does not prove a subscription ever connected.

provenance: Official Jito fork README, Cargo workspace, raw connector schema, snapshot source and Postgres target inspected at commit c18632c1b2dad92b3358acc22a5b4fa6fec55f1b; GitHub repository page identifies ckamm/solana-accountsdb-connector as its fork parent.
discoveries: The fork streams validator Geyser account/slot updates over gRPC and uses JSON-RPC account snapshots to initialize or recover a Postgres view; it exports account state, not complete transaction causality.

Its README exposes account-write and slot-update queue gauges and says sustained growth means the connector cannot keep up; it retries short database outages but exits after longer outages and expects restart/re-snapshot recovery.

The Postgres design removes older account writes as rooted state advances and uses per-node write_version plus rooted/confirmed/uncle status to select current state, so it is neither a durable full-history journal nor directly comparable across validators.

provenance: Official Solana Foundation rpc-latency-monitor README, Apache-2.0 license, example configuration, probe method documentation and metrics implementation inspected at commit f539f7f871fdb6fd15f1bb007ea72d605595e81d.
discoveries: The Rust service runs read-only RPC probes from multiple regions and exports latency, slot-lag, request-outcome and liveness metrics labeled by region/provider/method where applicable.
Its documented checks include getHealth, processed getSlot, latest blockhash and transaction/account reads; the README explicitly excludes transaction sending and landing-service latency.

Optional provider-claim checks compare selected results with a reference node, but are disabled by default and fail open when reference verification is unavailable; the per-provider rpc_up gauge is last-writer-wins across methods.

provenance: Official Codama README, root MIT license, monorepo package metadata, Anchor conversion workflow, visitor documentation and nodes package inspected at commit 252238f4f6165fafc46816077414fcef35d69e64.
discoveries: Codama normalizes Solana program descriptions into a Codama IDL and can convert Anchor IDLs before executing configured visitor scripts.

Visitors transform the IDL node tree and generate program clients or documentation; the monorepo contains separate nodes, visitors and renderer packages, including a JavaScript and Rust generation workflow.

Visitor scripts may load external packages and can prompt to install missing visitors, so reproducibility and supply-chain review depend on pinning the tool, IDL, visitor packages and generated output.

sources.overlap: Codama could support offline generation and review of protocol decoders already maintained in SYLPH; it overlaps existing Pump SDK use and custom wire decoders, so it does not justify a second runtime protocol layer.
risks: IDL can lag deployed program behavior or omit undocumented variants
